 Advertisement No physical copies of GTA 6 spark boycott fears and 'very, very excited' buzz
 Advertisement Updated: 7:03 AM CST Nov 18, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Carson DuRall Reporter No physical copies of GTA 6 spark boycott fears and 'very, very excited' buzz
 Updated: 7:03 AM CST Nov 18, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Carson DuRall Reporter OMAHA, Neb. — After 13 years, the wait for GTA 6 is almost over. It's possibly the most anticipated game of all time. While gamers are excited about the release, some gamers have a gripe about the way the game is being released. 
 "It's just a big cultural milestone. This has been like a big thing we've been building to for many, many years. And so people are just very, very excited about it," Zach Swoboda, the manager at Ben's Game Zone, said. 
 Advertisement "Everyone's like, can barely believe it with all these delays because it's like, is this this time for real? And yeah, I mean, it's already gotten nominations for game of the year. It's not even out yet. So the hype is just through the roof," said Ben Reed, the assistant coach for esports at Iowa Western Community College.
 A survey from BambooHR shows nearly 20% of workers plan to skip work to play the game.
 "I'm going to play it all day Thursday," said Ethen Gubbels, a student at Iowa Western Community College. Gubbels said he is not planning to attend classes on Thursday because GTA 6 comes first. 
 In 2013, when GTA 5 released, you were able to go into a game store and pick up a physical copy. But when GTA 6 releases on Thursday, that won't be an option. 
 "There are no physical copies of this game. If you go out and buy it, it's a digital code. Just kind of unfortunate," said Bill Ricetti, the head coach of Iowa Western Community College esports. 
 Swoboda said he is actually boycotting the release because of this change. 
 "I am not buying it on release. I am very much in the camp of I like to own the things that I play. I don't like the idea of me paying upwards of $80 to $100 for a game that can be taken away from me at any point," Swoboda said.
 Others are worried about how this new release will affect the future of gaming. 
 "I'm really, really scared for is if this does so well, then people will only go digital. And then that's that we have no say for like physical copies," Gubbels said. 
 GTA 6 launches this Thursday at midnight. So if your co-workers call in sick on Thursday, you probably know why.
